anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: At its approved L1, this is a small 3D block board with four visible target diamonds, blockers and hazards. The agent must use a single static view, rotate the board, and mine blockers before targets while preserving durability and inventory. Surveyors at L4 requires fitting three requested oriented cuboids among four distractors from a sparse point cloud, then matching every target to neutral marks across two frames and three views. Surveyors therefore has more simultaneous continuous geometry variables, target/distractor ambiguity, cross-view identity work, and link bookkeeping; the Mine's blocker-before-target dependency is meaningful but its layout, goal objects, and state sequence are more directly exposed.

evidence.explanation: The approved anchor is L1/simplified with four targets, one screen, one lava hazard, one support, and a small durability margin.

The grader replays rotation/mining and checks the exposed board constraints, rather than requiring multi-view cuboid fitting and mark links.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 task is one 2D hidden-target search. Cursor motion progressively reveals/converges a constellation through active visual probing, followed by one click; decoys and noise affect search, but there is no persistent multi-object fitting or cross-frame link assignment. Surveyors adds a 3D point-cloud interpretation, seven continuous box fields per target, distractor rejection, three projection matches per frame, and exact links. That is a substantial step above the L2 search even though both require spatial exploration and visual feedback.

evidence.explanation: The approved anchor is L2/full with one hidden target, two decoys, 26 noise stars, and one final accepted click.

The grader checks the mode-specific input source and one target click, unlike Surveyors' repeated seven-field fitting and mark-link requirements.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: Blind Dice Courier is the closest approved L4 anchor: its baseline has a long route through five gates, hidden die orientation after movement, and sparse scanner reveals, so later moves depend on earlier orientation and gate decisions. Surveyors has no evolving physical route or hidden orientation; it is a static multi-object estimation problem with continuous precision, three views, two frames, and identity links. The two tasks fit the same broad L4 burden for different reasons, with Surveyors stronger in simultaneous geometric control and Blind Dice stronger in state-dependent planning and temporal memory.

The grader replays moves/orientation and requires the ordered gate course and goal.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 Candy Cascade has four accepted swaps whose matches trigger cascades, gravity, and refills; every accepted swap changes the board and the legal/value consequences of later choices, while the exact score and no-forbidden-candy condition must be met. Surveyors has more continuous 3D fitting variables than a single board move, but its frame/view mark links are repeated independent obligations once the geometry is correct: linking one mark does not change the next frame or the cuboid. It lacks Candy Cascade's state-changing planning dependency, supporting L4 rather than L5 at the assigned baseline.

visible_baseline_solution: At L4/full, a screenshot-only agent must read the target list and point-cloud scan, use the visible initial cuboid annotations as a starting estimate, and reason about each requested object's center, extents, and heading while rejecting four distractor objects. It must use the cloud orbit/pan/zoom controls and direct visible handles to adjust seven fields per target, then inspect two frame tabs and three calibrated camera views. Each camera plate shows unlabeled depot subjects and neutral mark rectangles, so the agent must match the requested physical object to each mark from shape and projected location rather than from a shipped correspondence label. It must click the correct mark for every target and frame, link all 18 target-view-frame combinations, and submit. The grader requires legal event replay, center/extent fit within 0.16, heading within 8 degrees, 3D box IoU at least 0.62, and an exact expected link map; a failed adjustment can be corrected before submission, but linking one mark does not change the remaining geometry or reveal a new state.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The current explicit baseline is a demanding but coherent L4 static spatial-control problem. It is well above the approved L1 Mine and L2 Cursor Hunt because it combines 3D point-cloud interpretation, three continuous geometry dimensions plus size and heading for each of three targets, four distractors, tighter fit tolerances, and repeated cross-view identity matching. It is comparable to the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier in total burden, although Blind Dice has stronger state-dependent route planning and hidden orientation while Surveyors has stronger simultaneous geometric precision. It remains below the approved L5 Candy Cascade on the evidence available because Surveyors' frame/view links are independent repeated obligations after fitting, whereas every accepted Candy swap changes the board and future decisions. The L4 generator defaults are active and the explicit L4 controls leave their parameter map empty; this is not a middle-level default assignment.

evidence.explanation: The generator's active defaults for the unparameterized L4 profile are three targets, four distractors, two frames, density 18, fit tolerance 0.16, yaw tolerance 8, and initial error 0.30.

The grader replays the seven box fields and links, then checks center, extents, yaw, IoU, and exact expected links.
The assigned L4 control record explicitly selects the hard profile and leaves its parameters empty, so the generator defaults are the active configuration.

findings.claim: The authoritative grader does not bind orbit events to the selected interaction surface.
findings.causal_explanation: The browser emits orbit only from the Full point-cloud pointer-drag path, and Simplified pointer-down returns before direct orbit/handle processing. However, the grader's orbit branch accepts a finite delta and records no check against expected_adjust_source, unlike the pan, zoom, adjust_box, and link branches. Therefore a forged or wrong-mode orbit event is not rejected by the orbit branch; the source proves the missing guard even though this audit did not run a complete forged end-to-end transcript.

evidence.explanation: Direct cloud pointer handling is gated on Full interaction, so Simplified does not intentionally expose orbit through this path.
Full pointer release records orbit with direct_drag as its input source.
The grader checks expected_adjust_source for adjust_box/pan/zoom but the orbit branch at lines 160-162 checks only a finite delta.

findings.recommended_action: Require orbit events to carry the expected direct_drag source, or reject orbit events when expected_adjust_source is proxy_controls, before accepting the event.

concise_summary: Keep Surveyors Toybox at the approved L4/full baseline and retain the ordered five-level profiles. The source supports active increases at every adjacent pair and places the task above the approved L1/L2 anchors, alongside the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier for different reasons, and below the state-changing approved L5 Candy Cascade. Current-default versus explicit-L4 behavior matches at a fixed seed apart from identity metadata; historical preservation is unavailable. One source-proven orbit input-source binding gap affects all Simplified profiles and should be checked by the parent.
